name: Google LLC

jurisdictions.note: The Google APIs Terms of Service define "Google" as Google LLC, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California, unless additional terms for a given API say otherwise, and select the laws of California. This records the contracting party; none of the pages checked states where Gmail API requests are processed.

The Google APIs Terms of Service provide that, to the extent required by data protection laws applicable to the parties' processing of personal data under those terms, the parties agree to the Google Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms. Under those terms each party is an independent controller and Google Ireland Limited is the Google End Controller for European Controller Personal Data. Section 5.3 states that Controller SCCs are not required for European Controller Personal Data the partner transfers to Google, because Google Ireland Limited is in an Adequate Country; section 5.4 places UK Controller Personal Data transferred to Google under the Controller SCCs with Google LLC as importer.

euRegion.notes: Recorded as unavailable to the API caller, not as absent from Google Workspace. Google Workspace data regions let a Workspace administrator store covered primary data at rest in the United States or the European Union, on the editions Google lists. The setting belongs to the administrator of the mailbox being accessed; the Gmail API reference checked lists a single service endpoint and no region an API caller can select.

notes: This entry covers an application calling the Gmail API on a user's behalf under the Google APIs Terms of Service. Those terms apply the Google Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms to the extent data protection law requires, so Google and the API caller are independent controllers; no processor terms under GDPR Art 28 were found for this relationship, which is why dpa is recorded as unavailable. The Cloud Data Processing Addendum is incorporated into a customer's agreement for Google Workspace, so it governs the mailbox owner's relationship with Google, not the API caller's. Only aliases the cited Gmail sources tie to Gmail alone are listed: the service endpoint gmail.googleapis.com and the @googleapis/gmail package. Google OAuth endpoints and other googleapis.com hosts, and the general googleapis and google-auth-library packages, are deliberately not listed, because they are not specific to Gmail and host matching cannot see a path or a scope; attributing them here would file unrelated Google API traffic under these terms. They are carried by the google-apis entry instead, which names Google without naming an API.
